title: Settling the Premium Account of a Pass and Trip Protection Plan Given Up
content:
What the premium account of a Pass and Trip Protection plan is left standing at when a household gives the
plan up is what the unearned premium is set against, less that unearned premium, never below zero and rounded
to the cent; where the unearned premium covers what it is set against, nothing is left standing and the
difference goes back to the household by the route the plan settles by.

**What stands unpaid.** What stands unpaid on the protection account is the premium raised on the plan and the
charges raised on it, less the payments matched to premium entries, and it is never below zero.

**The unearned premium.** The unearned premium on a plan given up is the amount the return is worked out on,
taken for the part of the term still to come and at the share of it the plan returns, and rounded to the cent.
Where the plan is given up no later than its free look period counted in calendar days from the day the plan
was taken, the anchor day counting as day zero, the whole of the premium collected on the plan answers for
what stands unpaid instead of any unearned part of it.

**The amount the return is worked out on.** The amount the return is worked out on is the total of the
payments matched to premium entries on the protection account.

**The day the plan is treated as given up from.** The day the plan is treated as given up from is the day
cover began.

**The part of the term still to come.** The part of the term still to come is the instalments still to fall on
the covered holding's schedule as a share of all the instalments that schedule holds.

**The share the plan returns.** The share of the unearned premium the plan returns is nothing.

**What the unearned premium is set against.** What is set against the unearned premium is the charges standing
unpaid on the protection account, the premium standing unpaid being left on the schedule it rides on.

**The order of working.** The unearned premium is worked out first and in full, and only then set against what
is unpaid; the share the plan returns acts on the amount the return is worked out on after the part of the
term still to come has been taken of it, and never on what stands unpaid.

**Worked example (hypothetical inputs).** Take a plan carrying 195.00 USD of premium raised on its protection
account, 25.00 USD of charges raised on it and 60.00 USD of payments matched to premium entries, its covered
holding's schedule holding 5 instalments of which 2 have been charged. What stands unpaid is 160.00 USD. The
amount the return is worked out on is 60.00 USD. The part of the term still to come is 3 instalments over 5,
which is three fifths. The share the plan returns is nothing, so the unearned premium is 0.00 USD. What the
unearned premium is set against is the 25.00 USD of charges standing unpaid. The premium account is left
standing at 25.00 USD.
